task_specification.objective: Repair the candidate's authored spatial contract and ordinary five-wave lifecycle, while isolating a deterministic dense-profile qualification path for Tester recapture.

diagnosis.root_cause: Release convergence is blocked by three independent contracts: authored-world spatial binding and camera coverage still produce landmark/player occlusion, the ordinary five-wave route has only diagnostic victory evidence, and dense native qualification remains unavailable on the current llvmpipe renderer.

stop_conditions: Do not replace or destructively alter the preserved authored cemetery package.
Do not use diagnostic tester fixtures as ordinary-route qualification.
Do not claim dense native qualification while the required native renderer is unavailable.

strategy.rationale: Use a materially different strategy from prior camera transform tuning: restore one authored world datum with additive bindings, make route progression and upgrade application authoritative and replayable, and keep dense instrumentation isolated from ordinary release behavior.

code: Run focused Godot parser/static checks for cemetery spatial, camera, run-controller, wave, encounter, Bellkeeper, upgrade-draft, and dense-profile scripts/scenes.
Verify native_godot_project and host_godot_boot preservation checks remain passing.
Verify tester/validation InputMap actions are editor-only and removed from release exports.
runtime: Tester recaptures camera/movement/dash evidence at spawn, central landmark, cardinal traversal, perimeter, collision, and disappearance/occlusion checkpoints using ordinary movement replay.
Tester replays a clean ordinary run through all five waves, upgrade transaction, Bellkeeper phases/defeat, Result, and three Retry baselines; inspect authoritative route and build snapshots.

Tester runs three serial dense prepare/advance/reset cycles and records renderer classification, sample distributions, lifecycle cleanup, and runtime errors; native pass requires the eligible native renderer.
visual: Capture shipped gameplay views showing larger traversable scale, external world depth, grounded cemetery composition, central building/landmarks, readable escape lanes, and no camera occlusion drift.
Capture upgrade-draft cards at the target viewport and supported UI scale with silhouettes/icons, concise visual hierarchy, truthful current-to-new deltas, and keyboard/mouse/gamepad focus states.
Capture wave, boss, victory/Result, and retry states; inspect dense reset frames for visible corruption or leaked entities.

done_when: The arena has a larger traversable scale and a coherent external world/external depth beyond the playable boundary.
Every central building or landmark remains visible from spawn and cardinal traversal views; no disappearance or occlusion drift occurs during ordinary movement or movement replay.
Prominent structures and the boundary/perimeter have aligned collision; the player and representative enemies cannot pass through the central building or perimeter.

Spawn, objective, navigation, and collision anchors are rebased to authored cemetery streets/terrain without deleting, hiding, extracting, copying, duplicating, or repositioning authored child meshes.
Tester can replay spawn, landmark approach/near-contact/departure, cardinal, and perimeter checks with stable high-angle framing and readable dash escape lanes.
tasks.instructions: Repair the preserved authored cemetery integration at the world-datum/binding level rather than applying another isolated camera transform tweak. Inspect the native package bounds, then maintain one authoritative authored environment with additive outer datum, collision, navigation, spawn, and objective anchors. Bind the high-angle camera to that datum so the player, nearby threats, escape direction, central building/landmarks, and external world remain readable during ordinary movement and movement replay. Verify collision alignment, boundary/perimeter containment, and disappearance/occlusion behavior on all relevant landmark sides.
tasks.title: Restore authored cemetery spatial integrity and camera contract

done_when: A clean ordinary run advances through five data-driven waves with visible warmup, active, intermission/upgrade, boss transition, and terminal states; no diagnostic-only victory shortcut is used.

Enemy spawning stays within the playable datum, outside the protected camera area and safe player radius; all four ordinary archetypes approach, telegraph, attack, take damage, die once, drop rewards, and return to the pool.

The Bellkeeper is reached on the ordinary route, presents its telegraph and two phases with a recovery window, is defeated through normal combat, and transitions exactly once to truthful Result with Retry/reset.
Experience collection opens exactly one paused three-card transaction, preserves overflow, applies the selected upgrade before resuming, and changes authoritative weapon/build behavior.

Upgrade cards replace text-stacked choices with a visual hierarchy led by weapon or upgrade silhouettes/icons, compact stat icons, truthful current-to-new values, no more than three decision-relevant stat deltas, no NEW or LOCKED as a placeholder in the CURRENT value column, no unchanged or exhaustive stat rows, restrained copy, and complete keyboard, mouse, and gamepad focus states.
Tester can replay wave checkpoints, boss, victory/Result, and three clean Retry baselines while confirming selected id/rank/modifier in authoritative state.
tasks.instructions: Replace the incomplete diagnostic route with an authoritative ordinary lifecycle audit across RunController, wave director, encounter spawner, Bellkeeper, rewards/experience, upgrade transaction, and Result/Retry. Preserve deterministic five-wave timing, safe spawn/motion, exactly-once boss defeat/victory, and clean reset. Complete the real upgrade-draft presenter/controller as a player-facing visual hierarchy: replace text-stacked choices with weapon or upgrade silhouettes/icons, compact stat icons, truthful current-to-new values, no more than three decision-relevant stat deltas, no NEW or LOCKED placeholder in the CURRENT value column, no unchanged or exhaustive rows, restrained copy, and complete keyboard, mouse, and gamepad focus states. Any tester preparation hooks must remain editor-only, release-guarded, and separate from ordinary qualification.
tasks.title: Finish ordinary five-wave lifecycle and visual hierarchy upgrade choices

done_when: An editor-only dense qualification path deterministically prepares 25–40 active enemies, advances bounded motion for sampled frames, and resets with explicit requested/resolved/setup-generation/advance-generation/cycle receipts.
Dense updates use bounded scheduling or pooling, avoid per-frame allocation/leak growth, and retire enemies, projectiles, pickups, effects, timers, and signals on reset/end.

Receipts expose active counts, frame/physics/render timing distributions, allocation/orphan/error counters, lifecycle deltas, and sample availability without changing ordinary release balance or presentation.
The candidate remains boot-compatible with native_godot_project and host_godot_boot, and tester-only actions are absent from release exports.
Tester has a concrete probe surface for three isolated cycles; if llvmpipe remains the renderer, the result is retained as rejected software evidence rather than reported as native qualification.
tasks.instructions: Isolate dense-profile lifecycle and telemetry from player-facing route work. Extend the existing DenseWaveProfile/RunController/EncounterSpawner path only where needed for deterministic high-entity spawn, stable bucketed motion/presentation, pooling or equivalent reuse, cleanup, and auditable receipts. Keep ordinary wave balance and visual behavior untouched. Preserve the renderer gate and classify native versus software after samples are collected so the Tester can close the qualification issue when a native environment is available.
